title: Automated HEWL 24-well sitting drop crystallization on the Opentrons OT-2

containers.name: crystal_plate
containers.description: Stand-in for the Hampton CrysChem 24-well sitting drop plate (HR3-159) on its 3D-printed adapter. Reservoir (moat) wells are A1:D6 (4 rows x 6 columns, 400 uL each). The pedestal of each well is modelled as the matching well in columns 7-12 (A1->A7 ... D6->D12).

containers.name: HEWL_protein_tube
containers.description: Hampton lysozyme (HR7-110) 20 mg/mL in 20 mM sodium acetate pH 4.6, solution (2)

containers.name: water_reservoir
containers.description: DI water used to bring each reservoir to 400 uL

initial_contents.reagent: 15-Minute Lysozyme Crystallization Reagent (HR2-805): 30% w/v PEG MME 5,000, 1.0 M NaCl, 0.05 M sodium acetate pH 4.6
Hen egg white lysozyme (HR7-110) 20 mg/mL in 20 mM sodium acetate pH 4.6

steps.action: Set up the OT-2 with a p10 gen1 pipette (left, 10 uL tips) and a p300 gen2 pipette (right, 200 uL tips). Clip the 3D-printed PLA CrysChem adapter into two deck slots and seat the CrysChem 24-well plate in it. Upload the custom labware definition (A1 offset x 30.5, y 12.5, z 6.1 mm). Load the reagent, acetate and protein tubes and the water reservoir with source-tube geometry defined so the tips are not fully submerged. Calibrate the deck.
steps.source_quote: The machine was configured with a p10 1st generation pipet arm attached to the left arm, and a p300 2nd generation pipet arm attached to the right arm.
steps.note: Adapter and labware definition must be obtained or made and calibrated by the technician. Slot layout is free.

steps.source_quote: To prepare the reservoirs, 300–350 μL of solution (1) was added to every column (increasing by 10 μL every column).
steps.note: Column 1 = 300 uL. p300, new tip per well. The paper gives only the 300-350 uL range, so the 300 uL start is assumed. Volumes above 200 uL need two aspirations with 200 uL tips. Use slow viscous-liquid handling: slow flow, pause, slow withdrawal, blow-out.

steps.note: Column 5 = 10 uL (use the p10, which is below the p300 minimum). Column 6 needs no water (350 + 50 = 400 uL).

steps.source_quote: After all the reservoirs were mixed (discussed momentarily in the Results and Discussion section), the pedestal sitting drops were formed.
steps.note: The mixing method is not given in the text. Assumed p300, 5 aspirate/dispense cycles of 200 uL, tip kept off the well bottom, new tip per well.

steps.source_quote: 2 μL of solution (2) was aspirated into the pipet.
steps.note: p10, new tip per well. Dispensed into the pedestal of each well (A7:D12 stand for the pedestals of A1:D6). The tip is kept for the reservoir aliquot in the next step (same tip, per the paper).

steps.source_quote: This was immediately followed by aspiration of 2 μL of an individual well's reservoir fluid. The 4 μL sitting drop volume was then dispensed into the elevated crystal formation pedestal.
steps.note: Each reservoir well is paired in order with its own pedestal (A1->A7 ... D6->D12). Physically, the 2 uL protein and 2 uL reservoir fluid are aspirated in the same p10 tip and dispensed together as one 4 uL drop, repeated for each well. Modelled here as two transfers.

steps.action: Manually seal crystal_plate (the CrysChem 24-well plate) with Duck HP260 clear packaging tape after all 24 sitting drops have been prepared.
steps.source_quote: We then manually sealed the plate with Duck HP260 (Avon, OH) clear packaging tape after all 24 sitting drops had been prepared.

steps.action: Incubate the sealed crystal_plate undisturbed for 24 h at ambient room temperature (about 20-25 C).
steps.source_quote: 18/24 wells successfully yielded HEWL crystals in 24 h.
steps.note: The 24 h time comes from the paper. The temperature is not stated and is assumed.

steps.action: After 24 h, inspect each of the 24 drops under a stereo or light microscope and record per well whether crystals are present or absent.
steps.source_quote: green check marks highlight successfully grown HEWL crystals
steps.note: The scoring method is not stated in the paper and is assumed.

assumptions: The 24-well CrysChem plate has no matching container kind. It is represented as a plate_96_deep named crystal_plate. Reservoirs are wells A1:D6 (400 uL exceeds the 360 uL plate_96 capacity). Each pedestal is the matching well in columns 7-12 (A1->A7 ... D6->D12). The physical plate is a 24-well CrysChem plate (HR3-159).

Layout: rows A-D x columns 1-6. Reagent (1) is 300 uL in column 1, rising by 10 uL per column to 350 uL in column 6. Acetate (50 uL, 200 mM) is pH 4.6 in row A, pH 4.7 in row B and pH 4.8 in rows C and D. DI water brings each reservoir to 400 uL: 50, 40, 30, 20, 10 and 0 uL for columns 1-6, calculated from the stated totals. The paper only says 300-350 uL, so the 300 uL start in column 1 and the 10 uL steps over 6 columns are inferred.

Reagent (1) composition (HR2-805 15-Minute Lysozyme Crystallization Reagent) is 30% w/v PEG MME 5,000, 1.0 M NaCl, 0.05 M sodium acetate trihydrate pH 4.6, used as supplied (https://hamptonresearch.com/product-Lysozyme-524.html).

HEWL stock: dissolve lyophilized lysozyme (HR7-110) in 0.02 M sodium acetate pH 4.6 to 20 mg/mL by gentle rocking at room temperature, with no vortexing. It may optionally be centrifuged or filtered (0.22-0.45 um); the paper does not say whether the authors did, so record which is used. It is stable 24 h at 25 C or 30 days at 4 C. 20 mg/mL is at the low end of the recommended 20-100 mg/mL range (https://hamptonresearch.com/uploads/support_materials/HR7-110_UG.pdf).

The 200 mM sodium acetate stocks at pH 4.6, 4.7 and 4.8 are assumed to be made as follows: sodium acetate trihydrate in DI water, pH adjusted with acetic acid or HCl using a calibrated pH meter, 0.22 um filtered, used at room temperature (standard practice).
Reservoir mixing is not described in the provided text. Assumed p300, 5 aspirate/dispense cycles of 200 uL per reservoir, tip kept off the well bottom, new tip per well (standard practice).

Pipetting parameters are not given. For the viscous PEG reagent: slowed aspirate/dispense flow rates, a post-aspiration pause, slow tip withdrawal and a blow-out (Opentrons viscous-liquid application note, https://opentrons.com.cn/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/Viscous-Liquid-Handling-Automation-using-Opentrons-OT-2.pdf). For drops: p10 at default rates, 2 uL protein then 2 uL reservoir in the same tip, dispensed just above the pedestal surface with a tip touch, new tip per well (standard practice).

Pipette assignment: p300 gen2 (200 uL tips) for reservoir additions of reagent (1), acetate and water. The 300-350 uL reagent volumes exceed the 200 uL tip volume, so they need two aspirations. p10 gen1 (10 uL tips) for the 10 uL water additions in column 5 and for all 2 uL drop transfers. The tip-change scheme and deck slot layout are free choices (s2.1, s2.3).

The adapter (3D-printed PLA, spanning two deck slots) and the custom labware .json (A1 offset x 30.5, y 12.5, z 6.1 mm) released by the authors were deliberately not used. A technician must obtain or create an equivalent adapter and labware definition, measure the plate geometry (moat and pedestal positions, depths) and calibrate on the deck before running (s2.2).

Stock tubes and the water reservoir are assumed. Stock volumes are given as null (ample); the actual needs are about 7.8 mL reagent (1), 300 uL each of pH 4.6 and 4.7 acetate and 600 uL pH 4.8 acetate, at least 48 uL protein plus dead volume, and 600 uL water.
Incubation temperature is not stated. Assumed ambient room temperature (about 20-25 C) for 24 h, undisturbed, after manual sealing with Duck HP260 tape (standard practice).
Crystal scoring is not described in the paper. Assumed microscope inspection at 24 h, recording crystals present or absent per well (Fig. 5; the paper reports 18/24 positive wells).
The drop is physically formed per well in a single p10 tip (2 uL protein then 2 uL reservoir, dispensed as 4 uL). It is modelled here as two sequential transfers to the same pedestal well.
